([[Purcellville, Virginia]]) | college = *[[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]] (2018–2021) *[[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]] (2021–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 48 | draft_team = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | career_start = 2023 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–present | team1 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]]–[[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team2 = →[[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|Ontario / San Diego Clippers]] | highlights = * [[All-NBA G League Team|NBA G League All-Rookie Team]] ([[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]]) *Second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2023) *Third-team All-[[Atlantic 10]] (2021) }} '''Jordan Tyler Miller''' (born January 23, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason Patriots]] and [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]]. ==Early life and high school== Miller grew up in [[Middleburg, Virginia]] and attended [[Loudoun Valley High School]].{{cite web |last=Lukat |first=Carl |date=January 21, 2022 |title=Loudoun Valley grad Miller turns up the heat in first season at Miami |url=https://www.loudountimes.com/sports/loudoun-valley-grad-miller-turns-up-the-heat-in-first-season-at-miami/article_577342d0-7abe-11ec-8cdb-f300ac00b089.html |access-date=April 5, 2023 |work=[[Loudoun Times-Mirror]]}} He was named the Virginia High School League's Class AAAA Player of the Year as a junior after leading the team to the state championship and a 30–1 overall record. ==College career== Miller began his college career at [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]].{{cite web|url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2022/03/20/3-things-you-may-not-know-miami-basketballs-jordan-miller/7031393001/|title=NCAA Tournament: 3 things you may not know about Miami basketball's Jordan Miller|first=Eric|last=Boynton|work=[[The Greenville News]]|date=March 20, 2023|access-date=March 29, 2023}} He initially intended to [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] his freshman season, but became a starter for the second half of the Patriots' season following a number of injuries on the team and averaged 10.4 points in 17 games played. Miller averaged 12.7 points and 5.3 rebounds per game during his sophomore season.{{cite web |last=Furones |first=David |date=April 12, 2021 |title=Miami Hurricanes land George Mason's top scorer after losing several players |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-hurricanes/fl-sp-um-basketball-transfer-jordan-miller-20210411-r52nmmjrfbb63gx7xtcp6rj7pa-story.html |access-date=March 29, 2023 |work=[[Sun Sentinel]]}} He averaged 15.8 points per game and was named third-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference]] as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/miami/Article/Jordan-Miller-a-key-for-the-Miami-Hurricanes-basketball-now-and-the-future-183397117/|title=Jordan Miller a key for the Hurricanes now and the future|first=Christopher|last=Stock|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=February 24, 2022|access-date=April 11, 2023}} Following the end of the season, Miller entered the NCAA transfer portal. Miller ultimately transferred to [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (FL)]].{{cite web |last=Kaufman |first=Michelle |date=April 12, 2021 |title=George Mason leading scorer Jordan Miller transfers to University of Miami |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article250591569.html |access-date=April 11, 2023 |work=[[Miami Herald]]}} He averaged 10.0 points, 5.9 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.8 steals per game in his first season with the Hurricanes.{{cite web |last=Lichtenstein |first=Adam |date=April 12, 2022 |title=Jordan Miller to return to Hurricanes hoops team while Isaiah Wong remains undecided |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-hurricanes/fl-sp-um-miller-wong-20220412-cpxymamamfdofikf6kja2pcs2y-story.html |access-date=April 11, 2023 |work=[[Sun Sentinel]]}} After the season, Miller decided to utilize the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes who played in the 2020 season due to the coronavirus pandemic and return to Miami for a second season.{{cite web |last=Rufner |first=Jason S |date=January 24, 2020 |title=Miller time at Mason: Record-setting Valley star starting to shine in college |url=https://www.loudountimes.com/sports/miller-time-at-mason-record-setting-valley-star-starting-to-shine-in-college/article_71aeabb8-3ebf-11ea-bdd5-234416566fa7.html |access-date=March 29, 2023 |work=[[Loudoun Times-Mirror]]}} Miller was named second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]] as a fifth-year senior after averaging 15.3 points, 6.2 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.2 steals per game in 37 starts.{{cite web|url=https://miami.rivals.com/news/men-s-bb-jordan-miller-declares-for-nba-draft-plus-other-changes|title=Men's BB: Jordan Miller declares for NBA Draft, plus other changes|first=Marcus|last=Benjamin|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=April 5, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023}} In the Hurricanes' Elite Eight game in the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023 NCAA tournament]] against [[2022–23 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]], he made seven of seven field goal attempts and made all 13 free throw attempts as Miami won 88–81 win.{{cite web|url=https://richmond.com/sports/basketball/a-clutch-tip-helps-jordan-miller-miami-reach-first-final-four/article_f9f40ed3-d63d-5233-8da5-261f1073e686.html|title=A 'Clutch' tip helps Jordan Miller, Miami reach first Final Four|first=Tim|last=Reynolds|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 28, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023}} It was only the second "perfect game" with at least seven field goal attempts in NCAA tournament history after [[Christian Laettner]] had done so in 1992.{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/jordan-miller-christian-laettner-perfect-game-hurricane-guard-achieves-texas/md34ipg5bolnybbmts6dnuh1|title=Jordan Miller matches Christian Laettner perfect game: Miami guard achieves remarkably rare feat in win over Texas|first=Kevin|last=Skiver|work=[[Sporting News]]|date=March 26, 2023|access-date=April 5, 2023}} At the end of the season, Miller declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.upi.com/Sports_News/NBA/2023/04/05/Miami-Jordan-Miller-NBA-Draft-basketball/5301680716131/|title=Miami guard Jordan Miller declares for 2023 NBA Draft|first=Alex|last=Butler|work=[[United Press International]]|date=April 5, 2023|access-date=April 10, 2023}} ==Professional career== Miller was selected by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in second round of the [[2023 NBA draft]] with the 48th overall pick.{{cite web|first=Thuc Nhi|last=Nguyen|title=Clippers build depth by selecting Kobe Brown, Jordan Miller in NBA draft|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/story/2023-06-22/clippers-nba-draft-kobe-brown-jordan-miller|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 23, 2023}} On August 7, 2023, he signed with the Clippers.{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Clippers Sign Jordan Miller To Two-Way Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/08/clippers-sign-jordan-miller-to-two-way-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=August 7, 2023|access-date=August 7, 2023}} On March 1, 2025, the Clippers guard Miller agreed to a four-year, $8.3 million [[contract]]. The 2023 second-rounder had starred for the Clippers' [[G League]] team and acquired a standard deal, which included over $1 million for last 6 weeks of season. He made 37 total appearances for Los Angeles during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 4.1 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 0.9 assists. On July 8, Miller was waived by the Clippers.{{cite web | last=Sandle | first=Justice | title=Former Miami Hurricanes Jordan Miller Waived From Los Angeles Clippers | website=Miami Hurricanes On SI | date=2025-07-10 | url=https://www.si.com/college/miami/basketball/former-miami-hurricanes-jordan-miller-waived-from-los-angeles-clippers | access-date=2025-12-05}} On July 28, 2025, Miller re-signed with Los Angeles on a [[two-way contract]],{{Cite web|title=Jordan Miller Returns To the LA Clippers on Two-Way Deal|url=https://www.si.com/college/miami/basketball/jordan-miller-returns-to-the-la-clippers-on-two-way-deal|access-date=September 23, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}} however on February 18, 2026, his two-way deal was converted to a standard two-year contract.https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-jordan-miller-signs-two-year-deal/ Miller made 60 total appearances (including one start) for the Clippers during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 10.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 2.3 assists. On July 3, 2026, Miller re-signed with Los Angeles on a three-year, $15.3 million contract.{{Cite web |date=July 3, 2026 |title=Report: Clippers agree to 3-year deal with Jordan Miller |url=https://www.nba.com/news/jordan-miller-clippers-free-agency-2026 |access-date=July 4, 2026 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2023}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2023–24 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
